analysis:
Examined MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift BASE lines 1436–2081 and HEAD lines 1–518, plus the bounded change excerpt. These source excerpts do not overlap the changed implementation; no concrete regression is established. BASE media forwarding disables caching, cancels upstream on parsing failure, drains terminal events, preserves terminal usage/errors, rejects missing terminals, and releases model pins. HEAD retains separate coordinator/local schema-metadata settings (207, 275), request-local usage (321), audio validation before and after acquisition (323–333, 512), and native lease cancellation/release handling (375–446). No changed encryption, attestation, authorization, privileged execution, or billing control is visible in these units.
The patch introduces exit-thinking loop handling at HEAD 1024–1035, gated away from distributed pairs and requests with logprobs, and passes it into GenerationLoopGuardPolicy. This affects inference behavior under TB-007, T-007 and serving availability A-018/T-010; the policy implementation and the changed submission/forwarding block at HEAD 1108–1169 are not supplied here. Integration must verify that loop-triggered thought closure preserves answer/tool constraints, stop-string scope, bounded generation, cancellation and terminal usage, and does not expose withheld reasoning. Cache scoping (T-041) remains a relevant cross-file contract: HEAD 103–115 and 500–501 distinguish authenticated remote scope from local diffusion scope, but changed downstream handling is outside this batch. Review the remaining scheduler changes and related policies before concluding on security impact; missing source is a coverage limit, not evidence of an absent control.
